newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Mobutu departure clears way for peace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Mobutu departure clears way for peace.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said Friday the departure of President Mobutu Sese Seko from Kinshasa cleared the way for a peaceful resolution of the conflict in Zaire.

As rebel forces advanced towards Kinshasa, Mobutu left the capital Friday for his native village in northern Zaire and an official statement said he would no longer take any part in the government of the country.
"We believe that his departure now opens the way for a peaceful resolution of the military conflict," Albright told reporters before talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy.

"We are at this stage working with all the parties so that we can avoid bloodshed and also to do what can be done in terms of contributing to a process that would be peaceful and have an inclusive transition that would result in free and fair elections," she said.
"I think the most important point here is that Zaire now needs to move forward away from war towards peace, stability and elections," Albright added.
